Hi Sam / Marissa —

Following up with technical details on our access controls and support access (high level; happy to deep-dive in the call):

RBAC / least privilege:
- We provide a role-based model with built-in roles (viewer, developer, operator, admin) and the ability to create custom roles scoped to projects and models.
- Role assignments can be integrated with your IdP (SAML/OIDC) or managed directly in the Console.
- Default: support engineers do not have standing access to customer data or model prompts.

Support access / break-glass:
- Standard support: engineers operate on redacted metadata and observability traces; no access to raw prompts/outputs unless a customer allows it.
- Break-glass process: customer-initiated emergency access via Console ticket or SSO-approved flow. Requires two approvers from the customer's designated approver list (configurable).
- When break-glass is invoked we create a temporary scoped session token limited to the minimum resources and time window (default 1 hour). All actions are logged.
- Audit artifacts: session recordings (metadata only), command logs, request/response hashes (not raw content unless explicitly unmasked), and approver identities.

Logging & retention:
- Control plane logs: 90 days by default; can be extended to 365 days as a paid retention add-on.
- Support session logs and approver audit trail are retained for the configured log retention period and are exportable as CSV/PDF for audits.

Data residency:
- Hosted API endpoints can be pinned to us-east-1; dedicated/private options available for strict residency requirements.

Deliverables (I can drop these into the shared drive after the call):
- Support access runbook (support-access-runbook.md)
- Break-glass audit sample (redacted)
- RBAC role mapping template for FinTrust

If helpful, we can schedule a 45-min technical session with our security engineer and infra lead — propose tomorrow 10:00–11:00 AM PT or Thursday 2:00–3:00 PM PT.

-Vivek
